opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin access to Payroll. Admin is only permitted if the employee's role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. As an Analyst, the maximum permitted access is write, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB check: Erika Bolton (E002) is a contractor with basic security training (note says full-time, but Security DB shows contractor). Contractors with basic training may have at most read access for Payroll; write requires advanced training and admin is never permitted. Requested admin, so grant the maximum permitted: read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. The Security DB check identifies her as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have at most read access for Payroll (write requires advanced security training; admin is never permitted for contractors), and admin is not justified under either record since even a full-time Analyst does not own the Payroll system. Requested admin exceeds the maximum of read, so the maximum permitted level is granted: read.
